title: Joining Fletcher Henderson in the Big Trade
summary: In the winter of 1930-31 he went straight from Webb to Henderson, a swap he calls the Big Trade of Carter and Jimmy Harrison for himself and Benny Morton; he also recalls meeting Don Redman.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So then you -- would it be about right to say you left Chick Webb in '31?
Okay. Then went that same year with Fletcher.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. It was '31. The winter of '30-'31. I don't remember whether it was after Christmas or before Christmas, but it was the winter.
Did you go straight to Fletcher or --
Yes, I went straight to Fletcher. I closed one night at Roseland and went and joined Fletcher the next night.
Well, I got to know Fletcher. Of course
we all -- everybody knew everybody else, in a way of speaking, and -- but you must remember, like I always say, we were all uptown together. We weren't spread out.

Within a few blocks of each other. Everybody lived around the corner and down here and you'd bump into each other, you know, so I got to know all the musicians, not real well, some of them. It was -- and I remember that it was a real honor to me, to meet Donald Redman, even moreso than Fletcher Henderson, because he was such a great musician. Oh, he could play trumpet, piano, clarinet, saxophone, and one of the greatest arrangers, you know. That type of man is just a wonderful, talented person, and I thought a lot of it when I met him. Just wonderful. And then I met Fletcher a little later on, because he was sort of aloof. Fletcher wasn't a great mixer, like he didn't -- he became more -- more of a mixer later on, because I remember he used to come into the -- when I started working with Fletcher -- well, I'm a little ahead of my story.

The way he hired me, he -- I don't remember exactly how -- I just don't remember the point when he -- when he offered me the job, but this was a period where I call it the Big Trade. The Big Trade was Benny Carter and Jimmy Harrison, Jimmy Harrison the trombone player, they were working for Fletcher at Connie's Inn, and Benny Morten and myself were
working for Chick at the Roseland. So we made a trade. Benny Carter and Jimmy Harrison for Russell Procope and Benny Martin. So we switched jobs. That's what we always called the Big Trade.
